stories.headline: New York Still Giddy With the Bicentennial
stories.summary: New Yorkers, alight with the unexhausted spirit of celebration that has transformed their city into a great Bicentennial carnival for several days, refused yesterday to let America's birthday party end.

stories.headline: Queen Begins a Whirlwind of Activities in Washington
stories.summary: Queen arrives in Washington, DC, for 48-hr Bicentennial visit; is greeted by Pres and Mrs Ford as well as 21-gun salute; revs honor guard; lunches with Pres; to attend State Dinner at White House; other highlights of visit noted; illus with Pres and Mrs Ford and at Lincoln Memorial (L)

stories.headline: Market Turmoil; STOCKS FALL 156, LOSS OF 8%, AFTER BIG SELL OFFS ABROAD; JOINT TALKS ON DEFICIT BEGIN
stories.summary: LEAD: A new wave of pessimism overwhelmed Wall Street yesterday, prompting another big selloff in stocks.

stories.headline: 9-5 PANEL VOTE AGAINST BORK SENDS NOMINATION TO SENATE AMID PREDICTIONS OF DEFEAT
stories.summary: LEAD: The Senate Judiciary Committee voted 9 to 5 today against the nomination of Judge Robert H. Bork to the Supreme Court, and both supporters and opponents predicted his rejection by the full Senate if President Reagan continues to insist on a vote.

BACKED BY GENERAL STAFF Selective Conscription Scheme to be Submitted When War Resolution Passes. ARMY CALL READY FOR 500,000 MEN Careful Selection at First. Want 20,000 Skilled Men.
stories.summary: war resolution passed by U. S. Sen.

stories.headline: DEBATE LASTED 16 1/2 HOURS; One Hundred Speeches Were Made;-Miss Rankin, Sobbing, Votes No. ALL AMENDMENTS BEATEN Resolution Will Take Effect This Afternoon with the President's Signature. KITCHIN WITH PACIFISTS Accession of the Floor Leader Added Others to the Anti-War Faction. Miss Rankin Votes "No." The Early Morning Scenes. A Feast of Speeches. Levity Amid the Solemnity. Flood Opens the Discussion. Kitchin's Stand Surprises Leaders. Alabamians in a Rumpus. Why Wilson Must Sign Resolution. EBB AND FLOW OF DEBATE. Pacifists' Pleas, with Interruptions, Provide Chief Interest. Denounces Talk of Expediency. Cooper First to Oppose. Sensation Over Zimmermann Note. Rush to Hear Kitchin Talk. Cites Course Toward Britain. Why Not Forego Violation of Rights? Non-Partisan Plea by Cannon. Intimates Kitchin Should Resign. Only One Course, Says Mann. War for Human Rights, Gardner Says. Calls for "Vote" Futile.
stories.summary: naval, military, and industrial preparedness being rushed

stories.headline: SEEKS BOYS' ARMY FOR STATE FARMS; Agricultural Society Starts a School Census to Discover the Number Available. EXPECTS 5,000 FROM HERE Plans Laid to Make Work Congenial and to Give Credits as for Classroom Tasks. REDFIELD ISSUES APPEAL. Asks Commercial Bodies to Help Increase Crops. REDFIELD APPEALS FOR FOOD SUPPLY CALL FOR SEED STATISTICS. Pennsylvania Takes Steps to Organize Agricultural Army. GAINS IN FOOD PRICES. Commissioner Hartigan, However, Says the Supply Here Is Adequate. ROCKEFELLER LAND FOR FOOD Others Will Join Westchester Movement for National Defense. QUICK ACTION IN NORTHWEST. Minnesota, Dakotas, and Montana Increasing Farm Operations. GERMAN-AMERICANS BALK. Ohio Leader Holds Food Increase Would Help England. CORNER FOR JERSEY POTATOES If Present Efforts Succeed They May Retail at $20 a Barrel.
stories.summary: N. Y. S. Agricultural Soc. starts movement to recruit boys' farm army by taking school census; H. E. Cole explains plan for placing boys in congenial groups; Sec. Redfield appeals to commercial bodies to help increase crops
